data.title: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic, Meta to build data centres, Nikkei reports
data.description: Nov 27 : Japan's largest power generator, JERA, has entered into talks with Anthropic, Meta, and other US tech giants to build data centers near power plants in the Tokyo area, Nikkei reported on Friday.

data.title: Commentary: Black Friday is here, but what’s behind our need to chase bargains?
data.description: CARDIFF: Black Friday is a highly successful US export. The retail strategy designed to kickstart festive shopping has become a global phenomenon. But are the hype and the pressure (and the occasional fight over electrical hardware) worth it? After all, most products on offer during Black Friday are available at the same price (or even less) at other times of the year. So why do so many people still join in? Here are some of the marketing tricks and psychological drivers that help to explain the appeal of Black Friday.  MARKETING PUSH Offers that exist for a limited time period are among the oldest retail marketing tricks in the book. And there is plenty of research which shows that they reliably increase a shopper’s intention to buy. If we think a deal will disappear after Black Friday, the fear of missing out on a bargain can push us towards buying that air fryer or scented candle. Or we might buy it to avoid the potential feelings of regret that may come if we don’t. Price tags also have a big effect. Psychologists have shown that when making value judgments, the first number we see disproportionately shapes how we evaluate subsequent numbers. So when a price tag reads: “"Was £100 (US$131)! Now £60!”, the £100 figure is the one we latch on to. This makes £60 feel like a £40 saving rather than a £60 expense, even if the item was never really worth £100 in the first place. CONSUMER PULL While many people will be aware of these kinds of retail marketing tricks, they will still willingly participate in Black Friday. This may be partly due to its timing, but also to the psychological rewards that shopping could offer. In the northern hemisphere at least, Black Friday coincides with the “winter blues”, potentially offering a source of excitement as the days get colder and darker. We may also shop to improve our mood with a little “retail therapy”.One explanation for the effectiveness of retail therapy is that negative emotions often come from situations we cannot change. Making choices about what we want and then buying those things might help us to restore a feeling of personal control. Another reason is that buying generally might bring more positive than negative emotions. But studies have also shown that the temporary uplift from purchasing does not last as long as we often think it will. Landing a bargain can also make us feel good about ourselves. Being a “smart shopper” has been linked to a personal sense of achievement and pride when we secure a good deal. Buying things at a (genuine) discount can also demonstrate competence and good financial management to others. But that is not the only social appeal of Black Friday. Even the most independently minded consumer can be influenced by what other people do. And engaging in an activity at the same time as others, even among strangers, can temporarily enhance feelings of social connection.WHAT ARE WE REALLY BUYING? Despite the thrill of a bargain, or joining in with a commercial social event, what feels rewarding in the moment may not necessarily contribute to our longer-term wellbeing. Research in consumption has shown that spending money on things that fit our personality or that help us with personal goals might be a good idea. For example, an extrovert or someone looking to develop new connections will probably benefit more from spending money on social activities than buying a discounted item. But why we buy is as important as what we buy. In a recent study, my colleagues and I found that spending money in response to social pressure, to gain status or to seek others’ approval was linked to low wellbeing. So even experiences do not always bring more happiness. Our expectations can also mislead us. In another study I worked on, my colleagues and I found that people thought that buying new clothes would make them feel better about themselves than buying second-hand clothes. But it turned out that buying old and new clothes had pretty much the same effect. More broadly, research shows that focusing on economic gains and consumption brings a lower sense of wellbeing and is detrimental to our personal relationships. In contrast, choosing to live more simply or buying less is consistently linked with greater wellbeing. People who become less focused on material goals tend to become happier over time. So perhaps Black Friday should not simply be about how much money we are saving or how much temporary joy our purchases might bring us. Maybe it’s a time to reflect on what we gain from spending more money on more stuff, and whether there might be more sustainable and lasting alternatives. Olaya Moldes Andres is Senior Lecturer in Consumer Behaviour at Cardiff University. This commentary first appeared on The Conversation.

data.title: AI agents used in five cyber attacks in Switzerland, government says
data.description: ZURICH, Nov 26 : Five cyber attacks in the last few days in Switzerland used AI agents to target companies and operators of critical infrastructure, the Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) said on Thursday. • In four of the five cases, the attacks were successful and systems were compromised, BACS said in a statement • Three operators of critical infrastructure were among those targeted, BACS said • These included providers of electricity, water, and telecommunications, Swiss public broadcaster SRF said • BACS did not give details of who could be behind the attacks • Companies are being advised to establish protection measures, including regular cyber tests, it said

data.title: Temu commits to changing some of its commercial practices in EU, Commission says
data.description: BRUSSELS, Nov 26 : Chinese e-commerce platform Temu has committed to bringing several of its commercial practices in line with EU consumer protection laws, the European Commission said on Thursday. "Temu's commitments concern a broad range of commercial practices that mislead consumers or unduly influence their purchasing decisions, including fake discounts, fake reviews, pressure selling, forced gamification, and missing and misleading information," the Commission said in a statement. Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it would provide clearer and more accessible information for customer support, prices, environmental claims and checkout, and would make refunds easier. Temu also committed to ending forced gamification features, like spinning the wheel to access the marketplace, and pressure-selling messages, the Commission said. A Temu spokesperson said the company was pleased to have reached a resolution. "We appreciate the constructive engagement throughout the process and will continue to strengthen transparency and improve the shopping experience for consumers across Europe." Countries will now monitor Temu's compliance with its commitments. Failing to comply could lead to fines of 4 per cent or more of Temu's annual turnover in the concerned member states.

data.title: Chubu Electric penalises 13 people over Hamaoka seismic data misconduct
data.description: TOKYO, Nov 26 : Chubu Electric Power said on Thursday it has penalised 13 people, including former Chairman Satoru Katsuno, over the falsification of seismic data at its Hamaoka nuclear power plant in Shizuoka prefecture in central Japan. • The company asked Katsuno to voluntarily return 50 per cent of his monthly remuneration for six months, while two employees were asked to resign, the company said in a statement • President Minoru Yasui said the company had taken strict disciplinary action based on the findings of an investigative committee and a comprehensive assessment of the individuals' responsibilities at the time • The utility also submitted a business improvement plan to the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, including measures to reform its organizational culture and strengthen compliance and internal whistleblowing mechanisms • Chubu Electric received a business improvement order from the ministry on November 6 and was required to submit the plan • The company is seeking an external candidate for new chairman, to be appointed at its next shareholders' meeting, as well as a new head of its nuclear power division from either inside or outside the company. It aims to finalise the appointment of the new division head by year-end, Yasui said • The company also aims to formulate a new medium-term management plan by year-end, Yasui said

data.title: FIFA victim of cyber attack, files related to World Cup stake selloff unaffected
data.description: PARIS, Nov 26 : FIFA said on Thursday it had been the victim of a criminal cyberattack that gave unauthorised access to personal and business information. A person with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters that no files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. "FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information," a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. FIFA strongly condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, adding that such actions were "a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy". FIFA did not say how many people or organisations were affected, when the attack took place or what the business information included. Its reference to publication did not say whether any data had appeared online, or where. The person with knowledge of the matter said less than 0.1 per cent of the total data held by world soccer's ruling body was affected. FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in July that his organisation had scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors following a widespread backlash. The plan ‌had been to raise up to $4.2 billion by selling a 20 per cent stake in a new unit that would run FIFA events, including the World Cup.

data.title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after $6.3 billion crypto heist
data.description: Nov 26 : Binance said on Thursday its withdrawal recovery work is complete and it has lifted its withdrawal suspension after a record $6.3 billion was stolen in a hack last month. The crypto platform added that a small number of networks are temporarily paused while they undergo maintenance or planned upgrades, separate from its completed recovery work.

data.title: Dutch groups ask court to halt Meta smart glasses sales over privacy concerns
data.description: AMSTERDAM, Nov 26 : Dutch consumer and digital rights groups asked a court on Thursday to halt sales of Meta AI-powered smart glasses in the Netherlands, arguing they violate European privacy laws by allowing wearers to film people without their knowledge. While limited in scope to the Netherlands, a summary ruling in the civil suit against Meta at the Amsterdam District Court could set a precedent amid growing public backlash, venue bans and regulatory warnings across the world. A decision is expected by December 24 at the latest. The rights groups, which include the Netherlands' main consumer association Consumentenbond and Offlimits, which campaigns against online sex abuse, argued that the glasses developed by Meta and Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica both violate privacy laws and force people to constantly worry in public places, with a chilling effect on society. The plaintiffs want Meta to prevent its glasses from being used to record people without their knowledge, stop using recordings to train AI models and halt sales until Meta complies. They sought penalties of €100,000 ($109,600) per day per defendant for non-compliance, capped at €100 million. Offlimits' lawyer Karlijn Han said the glasses were used for what she described in court as "creep shots." "Covert recordings are undoubtedly also being made during exams, in changing rooms, at swimming pools, in hotel rooms and hospitals, but also in playgrounds and on beaches," she said in opening remarks. "Each invasion of privacy is worse than the last." META DENIES IMAGES ARE USED TO TRAIN AI Meta's lawyer Bastiaan Kemp said the court should reject the suit. He said the measures demanded would harm legitimate users, damage Meta's competitive position and amount to a product recall without resolving concerns about similar devices. “Providers of products cannot be held responsible for every instance of deliberate misuse,” he told the court. He said that a recording light on the frame makes it obvious when they are being used for recording. And he denied allegations made by Consumentenbond's lawyer in court that Meta processes images recorded by the smart glasses in Europe or uses them to train AI models in violation of European law. Meta and manufacturing partner EssilorLuxottica sold more than 7 million smart glasses in 2025, around 80 per cent of the global market. A lawyer for EssilorLuxottica argued that it neither processes nor has access to footage and that a sales ban would be disproportionate and ineffective given the availability of similar products from other manufacturers. BACKLASH EXTENDS WORLDWIDE From proposed restrictions in Australia and Norway to bans in courts across England, Wales and New York state, governments and judicial authorities are increasingly seeking to prevent covert recording and protect sensitive information. Cinema operators in the UK are also introducing restrictions over privacy and film piracy concerns.   On Tuesday, Germany's national consumer federation announced legal action against Meta and Ray-Ban over alleged privacy violations, arguing that the glasses make it nearly impossible for consumers to comply with European data protection rules when using them in public. The European Data Protection Board warned in October that smart glasses raised serious privacy concerns and called for stronger safeguards. Dutch privacy regulator AP this month advised consumers to not buy smart glasses, saying they are unsafe for both users and bystanders. In October, Dutch retail chain Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta's ​Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium. Meta also faces proposed class-action lawsuits in the United States over alleged improper sharing of private images gathered by the glasses. ($1 = 0.9124 euros)

data.title: US Marlboro maker Altria explores Imperial cash bid, possible carve-up
data.description: Nov 26 : US tobacco group Altria said on Thursday it was considering a possible all-cash bid for Imperial Brands and was discussing a deal involving part of the British tobacco group's business with another party, while Japan Tobacco was also reported to be weighing a bid. The moves potentially set the stage for one of the largest deals in tobacco industry history, combining three companies that together account for a significant share of the global cigarette market. Shares in London-listed Imperial jumped 13.8 per cent to 3,449 pence, giving it a market value of £25.90 billion ($33.93 billion). Depending on the structure of the deal, Altria could overtake British American Tobacco as the world's second-most valuable listed tobacco company, behind US Philip Morris International. Bloomberg News reported earlier on Thursday that Japan Tobacco was evaluating a potential acquisition of Imperial Brands, possibly with a partner, splitting up its assets around the world, citing people familiar with the matter. Analysts said a joint US-Japanese takeover could swerve antitrust objections and solve strategic challenges. The potential deal reflects mounting pressure on cigarette makers to find new growth avenues as smoking rates fall, and some struggle to compensate with newer nicotine products. Imperial said it had not had any discussions with, or received any approach from, Altria or a third party. "The Board is clear in its duty of aiming to maximise shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made," it said in a statement. Japan Tobacco declined to comment on Bloomberg's report. IMPERIAL'S APPEAL TO BUYERS Imperial would give any buyer a portfolio of established cigarette brands spanning Europe and the United States, including Davidoff, Gauloises and Kool, sold in more than 100 markets. A deal could mark a return to international cigarette sales for Altria, two decades after it spun off its international division to focus on the United States. That move created Philip Morris International. Altria has not sold cigarettes or most other products outside the US since, leaving it more exposed than rivals to several key challenges in that market. Altria has a market value of $126.89 billion, while Japan Tobacco, which sells brands including Camel and Benson & Hedges in more than 130 markets, is valued at roughly $69.45 billion. A deal for Imperial Brands would rank among the largest recent acquisitions of a British company by an overseas buyer. London-listed firms have become attractive acquisition targets in recent years due to depressed valuations compared to their rivals listed on other European or US exchanges. Imperial Brands trades at just 8.3 times forward earnings compared with 12.6 times for Altria and 17.7 times for Japan Tobacco, LSEG data showed. The mega-deal would add to this year's global M&A haul, which has been expected by bankers to rival the record-breaking 2021 total even after a pullback in dealmaking in the wake of rising rates. SEARCHING FOR GROWTH Japan Tobacco, Altria and Imperial Brands have all lagged behind rivals such as PMI and British American Tobacco in expanding beyond traditional tobacco, with past efforts yielding mixed results. "Imperial and to a lesser extent (Japan Tobacco) and Altria are in a tough strategic spot, without the financial firepower to properly compete with (PMI and BAT) as the nicotine industry transitions from legacy cigarettes," Callum Elliott, analyst at Bernstein, said in a note. Last week, Imperial Brands, which makes Winston cigarettes, announced plans to cut up to 4,600 jobs, or nearly a fifth of its workforce. Altria and Japan Tobacco already have ties, having launched a joint venture in 2022 to grow newer product lines. Japan Tobacco has also been expanding its US tobacco business, particularly in cheaper labels that have been winning market share - a trend that has benefited Imperial's brands. Under UK takeover rules, Altria has until December 24 to make a firm offer or walk away. ($1 = 0.7634 pounds) ($1 = 159.1700 yen)

data.title: SAP considers at least 10,000 job cuts in AI restructuring, Bloomberg reports
data.description: Nov 26 : German software giant SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-driven restructuring, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

data.title: EU may vote on authorising Tesla assisted-driving system at Dec 15 meeting
data.description: STOCKHOLM, Nov 26 : A meeting of European Union countries on December 15 on whether to approve Tesla's assisted-driving system across the bloc may include a formal vote by member states on approval, according to a draft agenda published by the European Commission. Reuters reported on Wednesday that a meeting where the technology would be discussed had been postponed to December 15. On Thursday, in a draft agenda published for the meeting, the Commission explicitly raises the possibility of a vote for the first time, saying EU countries will further examine the Dutch request to grant type approval for the system "with possible vote".  The vote is a key step in Tesla's effort to roll out the technology across Europe, with nearly a dozen countries having followed the Dutch lead. But ​EU-wide approval requires ⁠backing from at least 15 of the bloc's 27 member states representing 65 per cent of its ​population.

data.title: Polish defence ministry to sign agreement with Palantir on Friday
data.description: WARSAW, Nov 26 : Poland's defence ministry will sign an agreement with Palantir Technologies Inc. on Friday to buy software that uses artificial intelligence to support decision-making processes, the ministry said on Thursday. • No other details of the agreement were provided in a statement • Poland started cooperation with Palantir in 2025, when it signed a memorandum of understanding covering artificial intelligence, information technology, and cybersecurity

data.title: US Marlboro maker Altria explores Imperial Brands takeover in Big Tobacco mega deal
data.description: Nov 26 : US tobacco group Altria said on Thursday it was considering a possible all-cash offer for Imperial Brands and was in talks with another party over part of the British company's business, as Japan Tobacco also was reported to be weighing a bid. Shares in London-listed Imperial Brands soared as much as 17.6 per cent to 3,562 pence, giving it a market capitalisation of £26.77 billion ($35.07 billion). Bloomberg News earlier on Thursday reported that Japan Tobacco is evaluating a potential acquisition of Imperial Brands, citing people familiar with the matter. The potential deal comes as the tobacco industry grapples with long-term declines in smoking - its core profit driver - and challenges in building up new revenue streams from alternatives like vapes. Last week, Imperial Brands, which makes Winston cigarettes, announced plans to cut up to 4,600 jobs, or nearly a fifth of its workforce, as it tightens its grip on costs amid falling cigarette volumes and rising competition. An Imperial spokesperson did not respond to questions on Altria's statement, earlier saying it would never comment on rumour or speculation. Japan Tobacco declined to comment on the report. IMPERIAL PRIZE For any buyer, Imperial offers tobacco brands well-known across Europe and the United States, with its portfolio including labels like Davidoff, Gauloises and Kool menthol cigarettes sold in more than 100 markets. A potential deal could mark a return to international cigarette sales for Altria, two decades after it spun off its international division to focus on the United States. That move created Philip Morris International. Altria has not sold cigarettes outside the US since, though it has begun expanding internationally in newer products like nicotine pouches. Altria has a market value of $126.89 billion, while Japan Tobacco, which sells brands including Camel and Benson & Hedges in more than 130 markets, is valued at roughly $69.45 billion. A deal for Imperial Brands would rank among the largest recent acquisitions of a British company by an overseas buyer. London-listed firms have become attractive acquisition targets in recent years due to depressed valuations compared to their rivals listed on other European or US exchanges. Imperial Brands trades at just 8.3 times forward earnings compared with 12.6 times for Altria and 17.7 times for Japan Tobacco, LSEG data showed. The megadeal adds to this year's global M&A haul, which has been expected by bankers to rival the record-breaking 2021 total even after a pullback in dealmaking in the wake of rising rates. SEARCHING FOR GROWTH Japan Tobacco, Altria and Imperial Brands have all lagged behind rivals such as Philip Morris International and British American Tobacco in building newer product lines, with past efforts by Altria and Imperial to expand beyond traditional tobacco yielding mixed results. Altria and Japan Tobacco already have ties, having launched a joint venture in 2022 to expand in smoke-free products. "A joint bid for Imperial from Altria (only present in North America) and Japan Tobacco would neatly swerve anti-trust objections to a possible takeover of Imperial Brands," RBC Capital Markets analyst James Edwardes Jones said in a note. Altria said it was also in discussions with an unnamed third party for a part of Imperial Brands' business, although no agreement had yet been reached. Bloomberg News said the Japanese group has been speaking with advisers as it weighs a possible transaction, adding that JT has considered teaming up with a partner to buy Imperial and then split up the British company's assets in different parts of the world. Under UK takeover rules, Altria has until December 24 to make a firm offer for Imperial Brands or walk away. ($1 = 0.7634 pounds)

data.title: Japan Tobacco explores potential deal for UK's Imperial Brands, Bloomberg News reports
data.description: Nov 26 : Japan Tobacco is evaluating a potential acquisition of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The Japanese group has been speaking with advisers as it weighs a possible transaction, the report said, adding that JT has considered teaming up with a partner to buy Imperial and then split up the British company's assets in different parts of the world. Shares in London-listed Imperial Brands, which has a market value of £22.77 billion ($29.83 billion) according to LSEG data, rose more than 12 per cent to a nine-year high of 3,407 pence. A potential combination could create a tobacco giant worth more than $99 billion, according to Reuters calculations. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Imperial Brands declined to comment and Japan Tobacco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ($1 = 0.7634 pounds)
